strengths: Novel problem and first BoBW guarantees for heavy-tailed MDPs, addressing a genuine gap in literature with practical applications (network routing, finance, image processing)

Sound technical contributions including: (1) skipping loss estimators for occupancy measures, (2) novel heavy-tailed loss shifting analysis with local control, (3) suboptimal mass propagation principle, (4) innovative regret decomposition for unknown transitions
Rigorous theoretical analysis with detailed proofs; results recover sub-Gaussian bounds and match MAB lower bounds in special cases
Comprehensive scope covering known/unknown transitions and adversarial/self-bounding environments simultaneously
Clear exposition of technical insights and well-organized presentation with dedicated challenges section
weaknesses: Substantial polynomial factors in bounds poly(H,S,A) with unclear necessity; explicit dependence on (S,A) not well-discussed
Restricted to α ∈ (1,2] without justification; excludes α=1, α>2 cases and super-heavy-tailed distributions
Gap in regret rates for unknown transitions: O(log²T) vs O(log T) in known case not adequately explained; unclear whether fundamental or proof artifact
Completely missing experimental validation: no simulations, empirical comparisons, or demonstrations on motivating applications despite mentioning network routing and finance
Self-bounding regret bound (Theorem 5.1) is opaque with multiple W terms; no comparison table or intuitive special cases provided
No treatment of unknown tail parameters (α, σ must be known a priori); no computational complexity analysis; no guidance on practical parameter tuning
Presentation issues with notation overload (ℓ̃, ℓ̂, ℓ^shift, ℓ^skip distinguished unclearly); constants C, β defined only at proof end
Limited novelty in overall framework—FTRL over occupancy measures with Tsallis entropy is standard; main contribution is technical adaptation of skipping techniques

strengths: Addresses important gap: first to combine heavy-tailed feedback with BoBW adaptivity in MDPs
Novel technical contributions: skipping loss estimators for occupancy measures, local control of shifted losses, suboptimal mass propagation principle
Comprehensive results for both known and unknown transitions across adversarial, stochastic, and self-bounding regimes
Bounds reduce correctly to standard MDP results when α=2, supporting theoretical validity
weaknesses: Complete absence of experiments despite claiming practical applications—critical flaw for venue like ICML
Polynomial factors in H,S,A hidden behind Õ notation making optimality claims unclear and practical applicability questionable
Limited scope: restricted to tabular MDPs, requires known α and σ parameters, episodic finite-horizon setting only
Optimality gaps not characterized: no lower bounds for self-bounding regime; O(log²T) unknown-transition bound tightness unclear
Complex self-bounding regret bounds with unclear term dominance and potentially prohibitive dependence on ∆_min and C_sb
Dense presentation with limited intuition for key technical contributions; algorithms appear somewhat ad hoc
No discussion of computational complexity or practical implementation; constants C,β in Eqs. 16-17 would be burdensome to compute
Self-bounding assumption (Definition 3.1) is abstract; restrictiveness beyond stochastic/corrupted cases unclear

strengths: First BoBW algorithms for heavy-tailed MDPs with both known and unknown transitions, solving an important open problem that combines heavy-tailed feedback with unknown environment type
Nearly minimax-optimal regret bounds: Õ(T^{1/α}) in adversarial regime matches lower bounds; O(log T) in stochastic regime is optimal for known transitions; results recover Jin & Luo (2020) when α=2

Novel technical innovations: (1) skipping loss estimator tailored for occupancy measures, (2) heavy-tailed loss shifting analysis with local control of shifted losses (Lemmas 4.2-4.3), (3) suboptimal mass propagation principle for handling occupancy constraints, and (4) regret decomposition for unknown transitions isolating different error sources

Comprehensive analysis covering both known and unknown transition settings, adversarial and self-bounding regimes, with careful treatment of interactions between heavy-tailed estimation, occupancy constraints, and temporal dependencies
Clear exposition of technical challenges (Section 4.2) that explains why standard BoBW techniques fail and motivates the proposed innovations
Rigorous and detailed theoretical analysis with proper handling of complex interactions; proofs appear technically sound with careful use of decomposition techniques
weaknesses: Polynomial dependence on problem dimensions: regret bounds include factors like H^{1-1/α}S^{2-1/α}A^{5-5/α} which are suboptimal; limited discussion of whether these factors are necessary or can be improved
Log²T vs O(log T) gap in unknown transition case: additional log T factor compared to known transitions is non-trivial, but intuition for why this gap is fundamental is not clearly explained
No experimental validation: paper is purely theoretical with no empirical results on synthetic or real data; no comparison with existing algorithms even on small instances
Parameter dependency: algorithms require knowing tail parameters (α, σ); no parameter-free versions despite recent progress in bandits; no robustness analysis for misspecification

Self-bounding condition complexity: Definition 3.1 requires specifying gap function Δ and constant C_sb; final bounds have complex dependency on these quantities (e.g., ω_Δ(α) term); limited practical guidance on setting parameters or verifying conditions

Presentation density: paper is technically heavy with simplified main theorems but formal versions in appendix; heavy notation with multiple loss variants (ℓ_t, ℓ^skip_t, ℓ̃^shift_t, etc.); Algorithm 2 has many components whose interactions could be explained more intuitively
Limited practical guidance: no discussion of computational complexity, no guidance on setting constants C, β, D in practice, no comparison of computational requirements with existing methods
